newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Euro exchanges say phasing out Eurolist project.
newsitem.headline: Euro exchanges say phasing out Eurolist project.

text.p: Eurolist, the project to encourage companies to pursue multiple share market listings in Europe, is being phased out, European Federation of Stock Exchanges chairman Antonio Zoido said on Friday.
"We are in the process of phasing this out. There was not much demand for it," he told Reuters after a news conference on the federation's annual meeting held over the last two days.

The project, launched in 1995 by the federation of 15 stock exchanges, was intended to make it easier and cheaper for large European companies to list on other markets and issue regulatory and other information to their shareholders.
But Zoido said there was little demand for multiple listings as the highest turnover in large stocks tended to be on their home exchange.
He said that with the development of global financial markets, people could easily trade in the shares on the home exchange from their own country.
"The concept was a bit weak," said Zoido, who also heads the Madrid exchange.
He did not give a date for when Eurolist would end but a spokesman for the Amsterdam Exchanges said it had effectively ended already.
